multiplayer.title: Any client can win a Grand Prix without driving: lap reports are only checked against a 330 km/h floor
multiplayer.description: The server has each player's live position (`p.state`) and race progress (`m.g`) but `gl` lap reports are never cross-checked against them. `validLap` only requires time >= len / (330 km/h), a 0.9*min gap since the previous report and the cumulative sum to fit in the elapsed time. A parked car therefore sets pole in qualifying and takes the win in the race at the fastest lap physically allowed (63.2 s on Monza, ~20 % under any honest lap), which also starts the 90 s close and flags every honest driver at their next crossing. Confirmed with devtests/review-1/multiplayer/probe-cheat.js: 'forged quali lap accepted? true', 'cheat finished race? true rLaps 3', honest player 'fin true' after one lap.
multiplayer.failureScenario: A guest on a port-forwarded room (or the dedicated server) runs a 20-line script: after start, every ceil(len/91.67) s send {t:'gl', k, sid, time: len/91.67} while sending state g:0 from the grid. It is P1 in qualifying, wins the race, `winnerAt` is set, everybody else is classified behind it / flagged early.
multiplayer.suggestedFix: Validate a lap against what the server already knows: require the player's reported progress / lap count (from `s.g`) to have advanced by ~1 lap since the previous accepted lap, and require the car's reported position to have crossed the start/finish region; reject or hold the lap otherwise. Optionally tighten MAX_AVG_SPEED per track (the sim car's lap-time index is known from the seasons data).
multiplayer.evidence: Reproduced with devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-laps-progress.js (real server, manual clock). The cheater never sends a single 's' state; it only sends {t:'gl', time: 63.197} on Monza (len 5793, so the floor is 63.196 s against a real pole of 78.9 s). Output: 'after quali: phase grid grid [ 3, 2, 1 ] (cheat 3 ...) cheat rejections []' and 'cheater (never moved, never sent a state): fin true rLaps 3 rTime 189.591 order [ 3, 2, 1 ] winnerAt set true rejections []'. validLap (session.js 155-165) checks only the time floor, the gap and the cumulative sum. server.js 380-387 never looks at p.state, which stays null for this player all session. Lowered to minor: the game is client-authoritative by design (each client owns its physics, pose and lap timer). Exploiting this takes a deliberately written hostile client (Menu.setApplicationMenu(null), so there is no devtools shortcut). The harm is the fairness of a no-stakes room, and no requirement asks for anti-cheat.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: Tie a lap to the state stream the server already receives. Per player, add up the path length between consecutive fresh 's' poses, capping each step at 130 m/s x the arrival dt and resetting on jumps over 30 m. Reject a 'gl' unless that path since the previous accepted lap (or since the phase started) is at least about 0.85 x S.len, and reject any 'gl' from a player with no fresh state. This covers qualifying too, where no 'g' is sent, so the reviewer's s.g check would not help there. Also lower MAX_AVG_SPEED toward a realistic ceiling (about 300 km/h; no real track's pole average exceeds 265). None of this stops a client that fabricates a whole plausible trajectory. The social remedy is a host kick.

multiplayer.title: Impact reports let any player fling another car at 288 km/h 17-25 times a second from anywhere
multiplayer.description: The proximity check for `hit` uses the sender's own last reported state, which the sender controls freely (cleanState only clamps ranges). An attacker sends one `s` with the victim's coordinates (taken from the snapshots it receives) and then `hit` reports of magnitude HIT_MAX = 80 m/s every HIT_MIN_MS = 40 ms; the server relays every one. Confirmed: 17 relayed 80 m/s impacts in one second to a victim 1 km away from where the attacker 'was'. In free practice this works against everyone; in a race against every solid car.
multiplayer.failureScenario: Any joined player targets a victim id (ids are in every roster): the victim's car is repeatedly launched at 288 km/h, cannot drive a lap, and in a race is effectively DNF'd by a griefer; nothing in the log identifies it as abuse.
multiplayer.suggestedFix: Bound the relayed impulse to something a real collision produces (a few m/s to ~20 m/s, scaled by the reporter's own reported speed), require the reporter's state to be recent and continuous (no teleport of > TELEPORT m since the last state before a hit), rate-limit hits per target as well as per sender, and let the receiving client sanity-check the impulse against its own contact detection (it already computes contacts in collide.js).
multiplayer.evidence: devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-hit.js (real server plus js/collide.js, with main.js onRemoteHit copied verbatim). When the attacker's reported pose is 2.8 km away, nothing is relayed ('relayed ... 0'). After a single 's' placing it 10 m beside the victim: 'sent 22 hits of 80 m/s in 1 s, relayed 22'. The server checks only the attacker's self-reported last pose (never its freshness or continuity) and HIT_MIN_MS per sender. On the victim side, the HIT_MEMORY_MS de-duplication absorbs repeats in one direction: 'same direction -> applied 3 of 22; speed 60 -> -20 ... -100' (the car is thrown into reverse at up to 360 km/h). Alternating directions pass every time: 'alternating -80 / +80 -> applied 22 of 22; speed trace -20 60 -20 60 ...'. The victim's car becomes undrivable. For scale, a real head-on contact at 90+90 m/s asks for 108 m/s and a 10 m/s rear tap asks for 6 m/s. Lowered to minor for the same reason as forged-laps: it needs a hostile scripted client inside the room, and no stakes or data are involved. Among the gameplay-cheat findings it is the most disruptive one.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: Server: relay a hit only when both poses are fresh (under about 250 ms old) and the reporter's last pose is within about 10 m of the target's (collision BROAD is 8 m, not 60). Also ignore a reporter whose pose jumped more than 130 m/s x dt + 30 m since its previous state, and clamp the relayed magnitude to 0.6 x (|v_reporter| + |v_target|) from their reported speeds. Add a per-target limit such as total |dv| per 400 ms. Client (the main.js rewrite): in onRemoteHit, cap the summed |dv| accepted from one sender per HIT_MEMORY_MS window regardless of direction, so alternating directions cannot pump the car.

multiplayer.title: A Grand Prix started within 1 s of the host's second track pick is killed a moment later by the deferred pick
multiplayer.description: `track` picks within TRACK_MIN_MS are deferred to the tick, but `gp start` is applied immediately against the old `trackId`. The tick then calls `setTrack(trackNext)`, which ends the session it just started. Confirmed with probe-client.js: sequence seen by clients is 'track:monza, quali, free, track:monaco'.
multiplayer.failureScenario: Host clicks Monza, corrects to Monaco, presses 開始 straight away: everybody is thrown into qualifying and back to free practice within a second, then loads Monaco with no Grand Prix.
multiplayer.suggestedFix: In case 'gp' start, if `trackNext` is pending for the host, apply it first (`setTrack(trackNext)`) or refuse the start until the deferred pick has gone out.
multiplayer.evidence: devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-room.js: pick monza, pick monaco 700 ms later, start 150 ms after that -> '0ms track:monza, 867ms gp:quali, 1085ms gp:free, 1085ms track:monaco'. The same pick with the start 1.1 s later is clean: '0ms track:spa, 1107ms gp:quali'. So the server logic is inconsistent as described. In practice the window is tiny. Each track pick in a room runs selectTrack() -> resume(), which hides the menu (main.js 215, 232). The host would have to wait for the Monza build, press Esc, click Monaco and click 開始大獎賽, all within 1 s of the Monza pick. The outcome is also benign: the room ends in free practice on Monaco, the track the host picked last, and he presses start again.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: In server.js case 'gp' / 'start', refuse the start while a track pick of the host is pending (if (trackNext && trackBy === p.id) return;). The host's client then loads the new track and he starts again. Do not apply trackNext first and start right away, the reviewer's first option: m.len was computed from the old track's length, so the session would validate laps against the wrong length.

multiplayer.title: A > 1 s delivery delay on one lap report replaces the driver's summed race time with the server clock
multiplayer.description: `rTime` is overwritten by `(now - goAt)/1000` whenever it differs from the sum of laps by more than TIME_TOLERANCE_S = 1. A single lag spike on the message that carries the flag lap (or on any lap: the check runs every lap) adds the spike to the classified race time and gap. Confirmed: laps summing 40.000 s classified as 41.5 s with a 1.5 s delay on the last report.
multiplayer.failureScenario: Two drivers finish 0.4 s apart on the road; the winner's flag report is delayed 1.2 s by an internet hiccup -> his rTime becomes 1.2 s larger and the results table can show him behind (rTime is the first tiebreak for finishers on the same lap).
multiplayer.suggestedFix: Use the summed lap times when the sum is <= elapsed + tolerance (a late message can only make elapsed larger, never smaller) and only fall back to the clock when the sum EXCEEDS elapsed; or take the client's own goAt-anchored timestamp with the lap.
multiplayer.evidence: devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-session.js. A crosses the line 0.4 s before B, and A's flag report is delayed 1.2 s: 'A laps sum 60.000 -> rTime 61.2; B ... rTime 60.4; classified order [ 2, 1 ] (on the road: A first)'. Without the spike the order is '[ 1, 2 ]'. A mid-race spike corrects itself at the next lap because the check is re-run, so only a delay on the flag lap sticks. That needs a >1 s delivery delay (TCP retransmission, Wi-Fi hiccup) on exactly that message plus a close finish, hence minor. The reviewer's fix is wrong. The clock fallback exists for a driver who opens the menu mid-race: the game loop and his lap timer stop. Output: 'paused driver: laps sum 62.000, crossed at 92.0 -> rTime 92.05'. With 'use the sum whenever sum <= elapsed + tol' he would be credited 62.0 s and could be classified ahead of cars that finished 30 s before him.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: Have the client send its estimate of the server time of the crossing with the lap (gl.at = net.serverNow() at the crossing, which delivery delay does not affect). On the server, clamp at to [previous accepted at, now]. Keep rTime = sum when |sum - (at - goAt)| <= TIME_TOLERANCE_S, else use at - goAt. This keeps the pause protection and removes the latency term. Server-only alternative: use the arrival time minus that player's smoothed one-way latency from the heartbeat.

multiplayer.title: Live race order can be spoofed with a fake progress value
multiplayer.description: `s.g` is accepted unchecked and only clamped to [rLaps-1, rLaps+0.9999], so a parked car reporting g = 99 sits at the top of the live standings for the whole lap. Confirmed: order [cheat, honest, host] with the cheat parked.
multiplayer.failureScenario: During the race the HUD standings / gap display shows the cheater leading every lap until the honest cars' laps are counted.
multiplayer.suggestedFix: Derive progress on the server from the car's reported position against the track (the server knows the track id; ship the sample count / s per track or have clients send the sample index) or clamp g to rLaps + a plausible fraction based on elapsed time.
multiplayer.evidence: devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-laps-progress.js. A parked car sending g=99 while everyone has rLaps 0: 'order [ 3, 2, 1 ] -> cheat 3 first'. Once the honest car completes a lap: 'order [ 2, 3, 1 ] (clamp holds cheat at rLaps + 0.9999)'. So the spoof only puts the cheater ahead of cars on the same completed-lap count. That affects the live standings and, at the 90 s timeout, non-finishers on the same lap. It never affects finishers. A client able to send a fake g can already forge whole laps (forged-laps), so this adds almost nothing on its own.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: Fix it together with forged-laps. On the server, rate-limit the growth of prog: prog_new <= prog_old + (now - t_old)/1000 x 100 m/s / S.len, plus a small allowance. Optionally also require prog to have reached rLaps + ~0.9 before a race 'gl' is accepted.

multiplayer.title: No join secret and no idle/kick policy: anyone who finds the port can take and hold every seat
multiplayer.description: Rooms are joined with an address alone; a socket that says hello and then sends nothing keeps its seat indefinitely (ws answers the heartbeat pings itself; confirmed 'idle client still seated after 11 s'). MAX_PER_IP is 8, so two addresses fill all 16 seats. There is also no cool-down after a 'flood' kick: the same address reconnects at once (confirmed) and can repeat the 900-frame burst forever, keeping the host's Electron main process busy parsing.
multiplayer.failureScenario: A port-forwarded room is found by a scanner (or an ex-friend); the host's room shows 16 idle 'players', no friend can join, and the only remedy is restarting on another port.
multiplayer.suggestedFix: Optional room code checked in `hello` (shown next to the LAN address), a per-IP cool-down after a flood kick, and an idle timeout for players who never send a state message.
multiplayer.evidence: devtests/review-1/verify-multiplayer/v-room.js connects from 127.0.0.2 and 127.0.0.3, which isLoopback() does not treat as loopback, so the per-IP limits apply as for remote peers. Output: 'squatters seated from 2 addresses: 15; room size 16; friend -> full'. After 11 s of silence (two heartbeat rounds): 'squatters still open 15; room size 16'. ws answers pings itself, and nothing times out a seated player. Flood: 'flood client closed 1008 after 800 frames; same address rejoins at once: true'. The claim that a flood keeps the main process 'busy parsing' is overstated: the token bucket runs before JSON.parse (server.js 330-343), so dropped frames cost only ws framing, which any exposed TCP port pays anyway. Squatting requires knowing the address and the hello protocol (HELLO_TIMEOUT drops generic scanners). There is no host kick either. This is hardening for an internet-exposed room, not a violation of a stated requirement.
multiplayer.verifiedFix: Add an optional room code: the server generates it, the host UI shows it next to the LAN address, and 'hello' must carry it (reject 'code' otherwise). Add a host 'kick' action with a short per-IP ban. A per-IP cool-down after 'flood' / 'busy' rejects is cheap but of low value. Do not add an idle timeout keyed on state messages: honest players sitting in the menu before driving send only a ping every 10 s, and a squatter can send those too.

media.title: As shipped, nothing feeds the v6 sound / cockpit / telemetry / UI modules: no engine sound at all, telemetry shows a nameless car and 'N' in reverse, dead Q/E/T/M hints
media.description: js/audio.js, js/telemetry.js, js/cockpit.js setCar/setSources, ui.setCars/setPit/setAudio and F1.cars are complete and self-consistent, but the current main.js is still the v5 glue: F1.audio.init/setActive/update/beep/play are never called (the game is silent; the user's first v6 request), cockpit.setCar/setSources are never called (every player drives the default orange halo18 car whatever year / team they pick), pushHUD hands ui.updateHUD only speedKmh + a gear STRING ('N'/'R'/number) and no rpm / pedals / battery / tyres / team, so the broadcast graphic shows an empty team strip, no pedals moving, 'N' while reversing (telemetry num('R') -> 0) and a full battery for ever; ui.setCars / setPit are never called so the 車輛 tab says 車輛資料尚未載入 and the pit strip never appears; index.html advertises Q / E / T / M keys that onKeyDown does not handle. main.js is out of my scope and about to be rewritten, so this is recorded as the player-visible gap the rewrite must close, not as a defect of the modules.
media.failureScenario: Start the game, pick any track, drive: no sound; put the car in reverse: the bottom-centre graphic shows N; open 車輛 tab: no cars; press Q / E / T / M: nothing.
media.suggestedFix: In the rewritten main.js: F1.audio.init() on the first key/click, setActive(running), update(dt, car.state, listener, others) every frame, beep with the lights, play() for pit events; cockpit.setCar(spec, profile.colour) and cockpit.setSources({car, lap}) on car / track change; pass the full telemetry object (numeric gear -1/0/1..n, rpm, rpmIdle/Shift/Max, throttle, brake, battery|null, deploy, harvest, limiter, inPit, limitKmh, tyres, nextCompound, team, car, colour, colour2) to ui.updateHUD; call ui.setCars / ui.setPit / ui.setAudio; wire Q/E/T/M.
media.evidence: Reproduced in the real game. devtests/review-1/verify-media/probe-glue.js loads index.html with the current js/main.js in an offscreen Electron window, picks Monza, drives with real key events and wraps F1.telemetry.draw (log: probe-glue.log). Results: F1.audio is never started ({ready:false, frames:0, backend:'none', context:null, active:false}), so there is no sound. The object passed to telemetry.draw only ever has the keys 'speedKmh,gear,lap,lapTotal,curTime,lastTime,bestTime,x,z,heading,others', so there is no rpm, throttle, brake, battery, tyres, team or car. In reverse car.state.gear is -1 but the HUD gets gear 'R' (a string); telemetry.js line 656 num('R',0) turns that into 0, which draws N. Over the run 317 draws got 'R' and 141 got 'N'. After tapping Q and holding W+E, car.state.limiter stays false, deploy stays 0 and battery stays 1; F1.game.input only has up/down/left/right. The 車輛 tab still shows '車輛資料尚未載入。' with 0 cards, and #hud-pit is never shown. car.spec is '2025-standard' and main.js never calls cockpit.setCar or setSources. One detail in the report is wrong: the broadcast graphic HIDES the battery (no battery field means hasBat=false, telemetry.js line 665); it does not show a full battery. It is the in-car wheel display that shows 100% for ever, because E is not wired. Side note, outside this area: the page currently shows an error overlay '無法載入程式檔：js/seasons-data.js / js/cars.js', because other agents are still writing those files.
media.verifiedFix: Close this in the planned main.js rewrite (stage G), following the v6 glue contract. Call F1.audio.init() at boot and again on the first key or click. Call setActive(running) and setEngine(car.spec). Every frame call update(dt, car.state, {x, y+0.8, z, heading}, remote cars with their specs). Call beep() on each light change and on go, and play() on pit events. Call cockpit.setCar(spec, profile colour) whenever the car or colour changes, and cockpit.setSources({car, lap}) after every new lap counter. Replace gearFor(speed) in pushHUD with car.state.gear (numeric -1/0/1..n), and pass rpm, rpmIdle/Shift/Max, throttle, brake, battery (null when spec.ers is null), deploy, harvest, limiter, inPit, limitKmh, tyres, nextCompound, team, car, colour, colour2. Call ui.setCars, ui.setPit and ui.setAudio. Wire Q (limiter toggle), E (boost hold), T (next compound) and M (mute), plus the pad equivalents through mergeInput.

media.title: Engine keeps playing at full level while the window is hidden / minimised (the hidden-window fade is undone by the next update())
media.description: The module's header promises that a hidden window fades the sound out. visHandler sets stalled=true and closes the gate on visibilitychange, but the very next update() call unconditionally clears `stalled` and reopens the gate. electron-main.js creates the game window with backgroundThrottling: false, so requestAnimationFrame keeps running while the window is hidden or minimised and update() keeps coming. Confirmed in Electron with the real AudioContext (devtests/review-1/sound-graphics/probe-audio.js): stalled is true right after the visibilitychange, false after the next update(), and the master output measures -19.5 dBFS RMS (full engine) one second into the hidden state with the context still 'running'. A player who alt-tabs or minimises keeps hearing the engine (idle rasp, or the car coasting) until they come back.
media.failureScenario: Drive, then minimise the window or switch to another app (window hidden, page still ticking because of backgroundThrottling: false): the engine noise continues indefinitely instead of fading out within 0.25 s.
media.suggestedFix: In step(), only clear the stall when the page is visible: `if (stalled && api.active && !(root.document && root.document.hidden)) {...}` (and let visHandler reopen the gate on the visible edge), or have main.js call setActive(false) on document.hidden and setActive(true) on visible.
media.evidence: The symptom reproduces, but the cause in the report is wrong. devtests/review-1/verify-media/probe-hidden.js opens a REAL shown window, then minimises and hides it (log: probe-hidden.log). The page runs a rAF loop calling F1.audio.update, and the window uses the game's webPreferences (backgroundThrottling:false). Both while minimised and while hidden, document.hidden stays false, visibilityState stays 'visible' and no visibilitychange event ever fires. rAF keeps ticking (175 -> 1190 frames), stalled stays false, the context stays 'running' and the output measures -19.4 dBFS the whole time. So visHandler never fires in the game. The reviewer's mechanism (the stall is set, then cleared by the next update()) cannot happen: the reviewer triggered it with a synthetic document.hidden override plus a dispatched event. Control run (probe-hidden-control.log, backgroundThrottling:true): minimising or hiding gives hidden plus the event, and rAF stops (frames frozen at 176 / 322). stalled goes true, the context is suspended and the level drops to -200 dB, then comes back on restore. So the module works whenever the page is told it is hidden. In the shipped configuration Electron never tells it that (this matches Electron's documented behaviour with backgroundThrottling disabled). The engine therefore keeps sounding while the game is minimised, contrary to the audio.js header comment. The suggested step() fix (checking document.hidden) would change nothing, because document.hidden is always false. Severity is minor: the game loop deliberately keeps running in the background for multiplayer, and no requirement asks for muting in the background.
media.verifiedFix: Tell the page from the main process, since the page cannot see minimise or hide. In electron-main.js: on win 'minimize' and 'hide' call win.webContents.setAudioMuted(true); on 'restore' and 'show' call setAudioMuted(false). Alternatively send an IPC event through preload that main.js turns into F1.audio.setActive(false/true), optionally also on window blur/focus if the user wants muting while unfocused. As harmless hardening, also make step() not clear the stall while root.document.hidden is true, and correct the audio.js header comment to say that in Electron with backgroundThrottling:false the page is never reported hidden.

media.title: Steering-wheel display: the lap DELTA is never shown on a track slower than the previous one (lapBest survives setSources)
media.description: updateDisplay records a reference lap (time per sample) only when the completed lap is no slower than `lapBest`. setSources() (called when the lap counter / track changes) resets refLap, curLap and lapN but not lapBest, so the best lap of the previous track keeps gating the reference. On any track whose laps are longer than the previous track's best, no reference lap is ever recorded and the display silently shows the running LAP time instead of the DELTA for the rest of the session. Reproduced in node (devtests/review-1/sound-graphics/probe-cockpit-delta.js): 3 laps of 80 s on track A -> DELTA shown; setSources with a new counter, 3 laps of 100 s on track B -> only LAP ever shown; a 60 s track afterwards shows DELTA again.
media.failureScenario: Drive Monza (best ~1:25), then load Spa (laps ~1:45): the wheel display never switches to the +/- delta on Spa, however many laps are driven.
media.suggestedFix: Reset lapBest (= null) in setSources(), and also reset refLap/curLap/lapN/lapBest whenever the `lap` object passed differs from the one seen before (or when lap.n goes backwards after a lap.reset).
media.evidence: Reproduced with the REAL lap counter (js/laps.js), not a fake one. devtests/review-1/verify-media/probe-cockpit-delta.js (log: probe-cockpit-delta.log) creates one counter per 'track', the way main.js does (placed 10 samples behind the line), calls cockpit.setSources({car:null, lap}) and drives flying laps. Track A (80 s laps): DELTA is shown from lap 2 on. Track B (100 s laps): LAP only on all 4 completed laps and on the lap in progress, never DELTA. Track C (60 s laps): DELTA again from lap 2. Cause: cockpit.js line 1188, setSources() resets refLap, curLap and lapN but not lapBest (declared at line 1208). The gate at line 1286 (`lap.last <= lapBest + 1e-6`) therefore compares against the previous track's best lap. Impact: the steering-wheel display shows the running lap time instead of the delta for the rest of the session on any track slower than the previous one. The HUD timing box is not affected.
media.verifiedFix: In cockpit.js setSources(), also set lapBest = null. Better still, gate the reference on the counter's own best instead of a private copy: record refLap when `lap.last <= (num(lap.best) ? lap.best : Infinity) + 1e-6`. That ties the reference to the lap counter's lifetime and to lap.reset() (qualifying start), so no extra bookkeeping is needed.

media.title: Cockpit mirrors reflect only a baked sky/horizon image: cars behind are never visible in them
media.description: The mirror glass is a metallic MeshStandardMaterial with the 256x128 procedural equirectangular env map; nothing renders the scene behind the car into them. In a Grand Prix the driver therefore cannot see a car closing in from behind (head-look is capped at 55 deg, 'not to look behind' by design), which is the one thing a real onboard driver uses the mirrors for. The requirement is a 'refined and detailed first-person car'; the rest of the model meets it well (procedural liveries, live display, suspension, halo styles, 17 draw calls), this is the remaining functional gap of the first-person car in multiplayer.
media.failureScenario: Race with another player: they sit 5 m behind you; your mirrors show only sky and a grey horizon, the minimap is the only way to know they are there.
media.suggestedFix: Render a small (e.g. 256x128) rear-facing view every 2nd/3rd frame into a WebGLRenderTarget and use it as the mirror's map (one extra low-res pass, remote cars + track only), or at least draw remote cars as blips/arrows on the mirror texture from their relative position.
media.evidence: Confirmed from the code and a screenshot. cockpit.js line 750: mMirror is a metallic MeshStandardMaterial (metalness 1, roughness 0.06) whose only image source is the static 256x128 canvas from envCanvas() (lines 483-510: gradient sky, sun spot, blocky horizon, grey ground). Nothing in js/ uses WebGLRenderTarget, CubeCamera or setRenderTarget (grep finds no matches). devtests/cockpit-test/out/after/monza-start-halo18.png shows both mirror glasses with the same generic sky/horizon image. A car behind can therefore never appear in them, and head-look is capped at 55 degrees (cockpit.js lines 22-29). This is not a requirement the user stated: the original brief (docs/original-plan.md line 63) asks only for '後照鏡外型' (the mirrors' shape), and v6 asks for a refined, detailed cockpit. So it is a functional enhancement for Grand Prix racing against humans, not a missed spec item. Rated minor rather than cosmetic because in a multiplayer race the minimap is currently the only rear awareness.
media.verifiedFix: Optional enhancement: every 2nd or 3rd frame, render a rear-facing camera placed at the mirror / eye position into a small WebGLRenderTarget (for example 256x96). Use camera.layers so only the track, the remote car models and the sky are drawn, not the scenery, to keep the pass cheap. Map the result, flipped horizontally, onto the two glass meshes as an emissive/basic map instead of the env reflection. A cheaper alternative is a rear-proximity indicator in the HUD or on the wheel display from the remote cars' relative positions.

media.title: The own car's halo (hoop top 1.33 m) and the remote-car model's halo (0.93 m) are different shapes; the livery number is a hash of the car id
media.line: 944 (hp halo points, y up to 1.33); js/carmodel.js 143 (hp, y up to 0.93); js/cockpit.js 1165-1171 (number fallback)
media.description: The cockpit's halo hoop rises to y = 1.33 m (0.53 m above the 0.80 m eye point) while the remote car's halo tops out at 0.93 m, so the same car looks different from inside and from outside (screenshots devtests/cockpit-test/out/after/ext-front34-halo18.png vs monza-start-halo18.png). Also, CarSpec in the contract carries no `number`, so setCar paints `2 + hash(id) % 98` on the nose: a stable but fictional car number per team, not the real one.
media.failureScenario: Compare your car in a friend's view with your own: the halo differs; the number on your nose is e.g. 57 for a team whose real number is different.
media.suggestedFix: Share one halo point list between cockpit.js and carmodel.js (or scale the cockpit's to the real ~0.95 m); add an optional `number` to CarSpec (cars.js) and let cockpit.setCar use it.
media.evidence: The facts check out. The cockpit halo control points (cockpit.js line 944, plus the apex at 1.332 on line 947) rise to y = 1.33 m in a ground-origin car frame: group.position.set(state.x, state.y, state.z) at line 1330, eye at 0.80. The remote model's halo (carmodel.js line 143) tops out at 0.93 m. devtests/cockpit-test/out/after/ext-front34-halo18.png shows the cockpit model's hoop towering well above the car. The nose number is the fallback `2 + hash(id) % 98` (cockpit.js lines 1165-1170), because CarSpec has no number field. However: (1) nobody ever sees the own-cockpit model from outside, so the mismatch only shows when two players compare screens; (2) the contract allows remote cars to stay simple ('cars seen from a distance may stay as they are'); (3) the raised hoop looks like a deliberate framing choice for the first-person view. At the 70 deg vertical FOV the bar sits near the top edge of the screen, like a helmet-cam onboard (monza-start-halo18.png). At a realistic ~0.95 m it would cut across the upper part of the driver's view. The user's 'numbers from real data' request is about performance figures (docs/v6-plan.md decisions), not race numbers, so the fictional nose number is decoration only.
media.verifiedFix: No geometry change recommended. Do not lower the cockpit halo to 0.95 m without checking the first-person framing, because the bar would then cross the line of sight. If consistency is wanted, reshape carmodel.js's halo slightly (a taller, rounder hoop) so the two read as the same design. Only if real race numbers become a requirement, add an optional `number` to CarSpec in cars.js; cockpit.setCar already reads spec.number.

driving.title: car.js requires track.pit.paved(), which the contract does not define
driving.description: resolveTrack computes `state.onGrass = Math.abs(d) > hw && !(pit && pit.paved(idx, d))`. `paved` is a js/track.js-only addition (track.js line 1317 calls it "(addition)"); README-interfaces.md's track.pit lists laneD, wallD, inLane, contains, boxes ... but no paved. car.js guards `wallD` (typeof check in pitRuns) but not `paved`, so any contract-conforming pit object (test stubs, a mock track, a future track builder) makes car.update throw the moment the car leaves the road surface. Confirmed with a probe: a pit object with every contract field but no paved -> `TypeError: pit.paved is not a function` on the first update with the car in the lane (d = -12); with the car on the road it silently works, so the failure only shows up off the road.
driving.failureScenario: track.pit = {side, limitKmh, from, to, entry, exit, laneD, wallD, laneHalfW, wallHalfT, boxes, inLane, contains} (the README shape, e.g. the stadium/circle stub tracks of test/pit.test.js reused for a car test, or a devtest harness); car drives into the lane (|d| > halfW) -> car.update throws, the game loop's try/catch aborts the frame every step from then on.
driving.suggestedFix: Guard it like wallD: `var paved = pit && typeof pit.paved === 'function' ? pit.paved(idx, d) : (pit && pit.inLane(idx, d))`, or add `paved(index, d)` to the track.pit contract in README-interfaces.md.
driving.evidence: Probe devtests/review-1/verify-driving/probe-paved.js builds it-1922 with js/track.js and gives the same track a pit object that has only the README fields. Result: 'contract-only pit, car in the lane d=-16.60 THROWS: pit.paved is not a function'. The real pit is fine (onGrass false, inPit true), and so is the contract-only pit with the car on the road. car.js:705 calls pit.paved without a guard, while pitRuns (car.js:566) does check wallD. README-interfaces.md lines 486-498 do not list paved. The real track.pit also has length, boxLen and boxW beyond the contract. In practice nothing can hit this: js/track.js is the only producer of track.pit and always defines paved (track.js:1319). The stub pits in test/pit.test.js are only passed to pit.js, never to car.update. So the contract and the code disagree, but there is no reachable failure today. I lowered the severity from minor to cosmetic.
driving.verifiedFix: Add `paved(index, d)  // -> bool: on the pit asphalt (lane, boxes, tapers; never the road itself), from..to` to the track.pit block in README-interfaces.md. It is already relied on by car.js, test/car.test.js and devtests/pit-test. Do not fall back to inLane() in car.js: inLane does not cover the tapers before and after the entry and exit lines, so a stub would silently turn them into grass.

driving.title: spec.traction caps top speed: an 'accel' multiplier below ~0.97 lowers the car's top speed regardless of power / drag
driving.description: The drive is `min(traction, power / v)` at every speed, and `traction` is a constant per spec (the drivetrain cap), so the top speed is `min(v_drag_power, sqrt((traction - ROLL) / dragK))`. For the reference car the second term (337 km/h) is just above the drag-limited 330 km/h, so the cap is invisible; but the seasons data scales traction by 0.95..1.05 (README: perf multipliers), and a car with traction x0.95 is capped at 327.8 km/h at reference power/drag, and at 336.3 instead of 341.3 km/h with +5 % power / -5 % drag (measured with F1.carPerf; x0.9 -> 318.6 km/h). So a car rated high on top speed and low on acceleration loses its top-speed advantage; carPerf.topSpeed reports the capped value, so the racing line and HUD agree with the physics, but the car data's intent (top speed from power/drag, acceleration from traction) is not what the model produces. This is a coupling inside car.js's model, not a data error.
driving.failureScenario: Season car with perf.traction 0.95 and perf.power 1.05 / drag 0.95: expected ~341 km/h on Monza's straight, actually 336 km/h; a rival with traction 1.0 and power 1.0 (330 km/h) is closer than the ratings say. Any car with traction multiplier < 0.97 has a traction-capped top speed.
driving.suggestedFix: Apply the drivetrain cap only where it belongs (e.g. `drive = min(muTraction * an, power / max(v, 1))` with `traction` only as the launch/low-speed limit, or fade the constant cap out above ~200 km/h), keeping the reference car bit-identical (at TOP_SPEED power/v = 10.58 < 11 already binds, so the reference is unchanged only if the cap change does not affect v < 88 m/s; verify with test/car.test.js), or document the coupling for tools/build-cars.mjs so the traction multiplier is not used as the 'accel' knob for cars with a high topSpeed rating.
driving.evidence: Probe devtests/review-1/verify-driving/probe-traction-top.js drives car.update flat out for 150 s on a flat strip. The traction cap lowers top speed in the physics, not only in carPerf.topSpeed. Reference: 330.0 km/h. Traction x0.96: 329.6. x0.95: 327.8. x0.9: 318.6. With power x1.05 and drag x0.95: traction 1 gives 341.3, traction 0.95 gives 336.3. The cap binds below a traction multiplier of 0.9621 at reference power and drag, because the drive needed at 330 km/h is 10.583 against a cap of 11. The shipped data is not affected: all 12 cars in js/cars-data.js (2026) have traction >= 0.985 and none is capped. js/seasons-data.js and tools/build-cars.mjs do not exist yet, and the README allows multipliers of 0.95..1.05, so future cars can be capped by about 2..5 km/h. devtests/cars-data/model.js, the rating model, computes top speed from power and drag only (topSpeedFor has no cap), so a generator that reuses it would disagree with car.js for those cars. The same mechanism also applies to tyres: car.js:470 multiplies the whole min(K.traction, muTraction*an) by tyres.grip.traction, so the constant drivetrain cap shrinks as the tyres wear. Probe probe-tyre-wear-top.js with the real js/tyres.js gives these rear-wear results. 75% wear: grip 0.960, 329.6 km/h. 85%: 0.921, 322 km/h. 90%: 0.877, 314 km/h. 99%: 0.717, 282 km/h. A stub with grip.traction 0.9 gives 318.6 km/h in the physics, while carPerf.topSpeed, which the racing line uses, still says 330. This contradicts tyres.js's own note (line 15) that at speed the drivetrain, not the tyres, limits traction.
driving.verifiedFix: Two changes, both bit-identical for the reference car on new mediums. (1) Scale only the friction term by the tyre multiplier: `Math.min(K.traction, K.muTraction * an * gTrac)` in stepPhysics. Worn or dirty tyres then cost traction at low speed but no longer top speed. Softs lose their +1.5% launch traction, which is acceptable or can be re-tuned. (2) For spec.traction, either make the drivetrain cap rise above the reference's crossover speed V_X = POWER/TRACTION = 88.2 m/s, e.g. cap = K.traction * max(1, (av / V_X)^2). For the reference P/v <= 11 above V_X, so nothing changes, and traction multipliers down to about 0.9 no longer cap top speed. Apply the same change in carPerf.maxAccel, topFor and topBoost. Or, at minimum, have tools/build-cars.mjs compute topSpeed ratings and estimates from F1.carPerf(spec).topSpeed, which includes the cap, rather than from a power/drag-only formula. Check with test/car.test.js (golden rule against car-v5).

driving.title: Car-to-car impacts never reach the tyre model (no flat spots / punctures from contact with other cars)
driving.description: update() sets `state.hit = 0` first and feeds `load.hit = state.hit` to tyres.update inside its sub-step loop, so only impacts produced by car.js itself (outer walls, pit wall) are seen by js/tyres.js. F1.resolveCarCollisions / F1.applyCarImpulse set state.hit AFTER car.update (main.js line 722 / 733), and the next car.update clears it before the tyres see it. The tyre header promises flat spots and punctures from 'a hard impact' / 'a very heavy impact'; head-on car contact at any closing speed leaves the tyres untouched, while the same hit against a wall gives an 80 % puncture chance at hit 1.
driving.failureScenario: Race: driver A rams driver B at a 100 km/h closing speed (collide hit = 0.93). Both cars bounce, rumble and shake, but neither car's tyres get a flat spot or a puncture; the same impact against the pit wall would puncture with p = 0.7.
driving.suggestedFix: Let car.update take the impacts resolved since the last step into account: e.g. keep an `extHit` the caller sets (car.reportHit(h)) that is merged into load.hit on the next sub-step, or make the tyres a step of their own that main.js feeds with the frame's strongest hit.
driving.evidence: Probe devtests/review-1/verify-driving/probe-car-hit-tyres.js follows the main.js order (main.js:720-733): car.update, then F1.resolveCarCollisions, then car.state.hit set to the frame's hit. Over 200 seeds, a car at 100 km/h hits a stopped car (hit up to 1.000) and gets 0 flat spots and 0 punctures. The same car hitting a wall at 40 m/s and 45 deg (hit 0.944) gets 200 flat spots and 150 punctures. Cause: car.update sets state.hit = 0 first (car.js:722) and passes load.hit = state.hit to tyres.update only inside its own sub-steps (car.js:744). The hits from collide.js, set after car.update, are wiped before the tyres see them. Note: README line 46 defines car.state.hit as 'wall impact strength', so this is a gap against the tyre header ('a hard impact' / 'a very heavy impact') and the several-kinds-of-tyre-damage request, not a contract violation. The current main.js is v5 and has no tyres wiring yet.
driving.verifiedFix: Give car.js an explicit external impact: `car.addImpact(h)` keeps `extHit = max(extHit, h)`, and the next sub-step feeds `load.hit = max(state.hit, extHit)` and clears extHit. In the main.js rewrite, call it with the return value of F1.resolveCarCollisions, which is local detection and symmetric on both clients. Do not feed it the network-reported F1.applyCarImpulse hits: a hostile client could otherwise send impulses to puncture other cars. Do not simply stop clearing state.hit. main.js writes the frame's strongest hit, including wall hits the tyres already saw, back into state.hit, and at low frame rates the tyres' hitPeak decay (2/s) would count it as a new impact.

driving.title: sanitizeSpec: ers 0 / '' / {} silently gives the reference battery instead of 'no ERS'
driving.description: Only `ers === null || ers === false` means 'no battery'; any other falsy or malformed value (0, '', {}, 'x') becomes the full reference ERS {store 4656.67, power 145.5, harvest 230}. A generated data file that encodes 'no KERS' as `ers: 0` (2010, or any pre-2009 style entry) would give that car a 2025-spec battery. Documented in the header comment, but the failure is silent (verified: `sanitizeSpec({ers: 0}).ers` = reference ERS).
driving.failureScenario: seasons-data era with `ers: 0` -> every car of that season deploys +145 W/kg on E, HUD shows a battery.
driving.suggestedFix: Treat any falsy `ers` (and any non-object) as null, or log/throw on malformed ers in tools/build-cars.mjs.
driving.evidence: Probe devtests/review-1/verify-driving/probe-ers.js: ers 0, '', NaN, {}, 'x' and {store:0, power:0, harvest:0} all become the reference battery {store 4656.67, power 145.52, harvest 230}, with battery 1 and topSpeedBoost 346.2 km/h. Only null and false give no battery (330.0 km/h). The all-zero object is the most plausible way a generator would encode a 2010 car, since tools/eras.json has powerElectric 0 kW for 2010, and it silently gets a 2025 battery. The behaviour is documented in car.js ('missing = the reference's'), and ers: 0 is outside the contract type (null | {...}). No current data triggers it: js/seasons-data.js is not generated yet and js/cars-data.js is all 2026 hybrid cars.
driving.verifiedFix: In sanitizeSpec: `if (e === undefined) -> the reference's; else if (!e || typeof e !== 'object' || e.power === 0 || e.store === 0) -> null; else per-field range check as now`. This keeps the existing assertions in test/car.test.js:334-346 passing: {} and undefined give the reference battery, and {store:-1, power:'big', ...} is still reset to the reference. Also have tools/build-cars.mjs write ers: null for seasons without KERS or ERS.

world.title: Pit building texture shows a second row of garage doors and numbers above the garage face on sloping pit straights
world.description: A real (OSM) pit building and each procedural block get ONE reference height (pitRefY = the highest lane height under the footprint; slab y = max over the block) and the pit texture (garage openings 0.2-4.5 m, number fascia 4.8-5.6 m above ref) is mapped from it. Where the pit lane slopes, the downhill end of the building is measured from a level up to several metres above the local lane, so the texture's garage openings and numbered fascia rise above the 6 m garage face of js/track.js and a second, textured row of garages sits on top of the real one. Measured (fascia top above the face): Hungaroring 4.4 m, Spa 4.8 m, Zandvoort 2.0 m, Suzuka 1.5 m; COTA / Red Bull Ring 0. Confirmed in the render devtests/review-1/world/out/probe-hu-1986-box8-perp.png (dark openings + '9 8 9 8' fascia above the face) and in hu-1986-approach / nl-1948-exit.
world.failureScenario: Drive into the Hungaroring pit lane (side -1, lane drops 10 m over its length): beside boxes 1-8 the garage face is topped by a second row of black garage openings with team numbers, then the glazing.
world.suggestedFix: Give the texture a per-vertex reference: compute v from the local lane height at each wall vertex (sY at the nearest sample) instead of one ref per polygon, or split real pit buildings into ~30 m segments like the procedural blocks; alternatively draw the garage openings/fascia only where ref - localLane < 0.5 m and put the openings at v below the 6 m face for the rest.
world.evidence: Code: scenery.js addBuilding (984, 995) maps the pit texture with one ref per polygon (v = (y - ref)/10). pitRefY (1173-1183) takes the HIGHEST lane height under a real OSM pit footprint, and slab() (1429) takes the max over a ~30 m procedural block. texPit rows put the garage opening 0.23-4.53 m and the fascia 4.77-5.63 m above ref; the track.js garage face is 6 m (PIT_GARAGE_H). Probe devtests/review-1/verify-world/pit-tex.js reads ref = y - 10*v straight off every vertex of the built 'scenery-pit' mesh on the building front (1-3 m behind the face, beside the full-depth face) and compares it with track.surfaceY at the face (log: out/pit-tex.log). Measured delta = ref - local lane: my-1999 5.64 m (fascia top 5.26 m above the face, garage openings 4.17 m above it), be-1925 5.16 (4.79), hu-1986 4.74 (4.36), br-1940 4.34 (3.96), it-1914 2.78, pt-1972 2.72, pt-2008 2.36, mx-1962 2.09, fr-1960 2.01, fr-1969 2.00, jp-1962 1.82 (1.44), de-1932 1.62. Tracks with no visible problem: us-2012 -0.12, at-1969 0.02, nl-1948 -0.07. Zandvoort only reaches 2.0 m in the ramp zone at the end of the face (wider filter). Electron renders (verify-world/shot.js) out/my-1999-pit-perp.png and out/my-1999-pit-along.png, taken from the lane at 1 m eye height, show a second row of black garage openings with numbered red/blue fascia ('9', '16') on top of the track.js garage face. So the reviewer's Hungaroring and Spa figures reproduce exactly, and the defect is worse at Sepang.
world.verifiedFix: In scenery.js addBuilding, for style 2 (pit) walls with a yRef, use a per-vertex texture reference instead of one ref per polygon. Densify the footprint edges to <= 4 m. For each vertex compute refV = sY(s, pitSide*wallD(s, pitSide)) at its nearest pit sample s, clamped to the lane heights of pitMask, and emit each quad with its own v per end: vb = (base - refV)/10, vt = (top - refV)/10 (quad() directly, since wall() takes a single vb/vt). Keep top = max(refV) + h so the roof stays flat. The garage/fascia rows then stay hidden behind the 6 m face everywhere, and only the glazing shows above it. Splitting long real pit footprints into ~30 m chunks is a weaker alternative.

world.title: Banking is derived from curvature (max 6 deg), so real banked corners (Zandvoort 18-19 deg, Indianapolis oval 9 deg) do not exist
world.description: The user asked for real elevation AND banking. Elevation comes from a DEM, but bank[i] = -BANK_MAX * tanh(BANK_GAIN * curv) capped at 6 degrees, i.e. every corner of every track is banked by the same formula (inside lower). tracks-data.js carries no banking. Zandvoort's Hugenholtz (T3) and Arie Luyendyk (T14) bowls are 18-19 deg in reality and the Indianapolis oval turns 9 deg; the probe over all 40 tracks shows max |bank| 5.2-6.0 deg everywhere (Zandvoort 5.6). The cockpit renders nl-1948-c4/c5 show flat-looking corners.
world.failureScenario: Select Circuit Zandvoort and drive T3 or the final corner: the road tilts at most ~6 deg like any other bend; the banked bowls the user expects are missing, and lap physics through them is wrong.
world.suggestedFix: Add a per-track (or per-segment) banking table to tracks-data.js (few tracks need it: Zandvoort T3/T14, Indianapolis oval, Monza old banking not used) and let track.js use it in place of the curvature formula where present.
world.evidence: Code: track.js 400-412, bankRaw = -BANK_MAX*tanh(BANK_GAIN*curv/BANK_MAX) with BANK_MAX = 6 deg, then smoothed. No other source exists: tracks-data.js has only id,name,location,lengthKm,geo,points,elev (checked all 40 entries), and tools/build-tracks.mjs emits no banking. Probe verify-world/bank.js (out/bank.log): whole-lap max |bank| is nl-1948 5.62 deg, us-1909 5.64, sa-2021 5.69, and 5.96 deg (de-1932) is the highest over all 40 tracks. The per-corner listing shows Zandvoort's corner runs peaking at 1.0-5.6 deg; the final banked right-hander run (3707-3983 m) reaches 2.6 deg. Real values are about 19 deg (Hugenholtz), 18 deg (Luyendyk), about 9 deg (Indianapolis oval turn) and about 12 deg (Jeddah T13). The formula also banks every bend inside-low, including real flat and off-camber corners. The user explicitly asked for real banking, and it is absent exactly at the corners where banking is noticeable. Since car.js physics uses bank, corner speeds there are wrong as well as the look.
world.verifiedFix: Add real banking only where it matters, as data. In tools/build-tracks.mjs (or a small table in track.js keyed by track id), list segments {s0, s1, bankDeg}, for example nl-1948 T3 ~19 deg and T14 ~18 deg, us-1909 oval turn ~9 deg, sa-2021 T13 ~12 deg; add others if found. In track.js, blend bankRaw towards the table value over the segment with a smoothstep ramp of ~30-40 m, bypassing the 6 deg cap there. Consider reducing the generic formula elsewhere (e.g. cap 3 deg) so ordinary corners are not over-banked. Re-run the raceline drive test, since corner speeds change.

world.title: Elevation profile: COTA too flat (20.6 m vs ~41 m real), Monaco exaggerated (54 m vs ~42 m), Las Vegas hilly (25 m, 8.7 % grades) though the Strip is flat
world.line: elev arrays (generated by tools/build-tracks.mjs, MEDIAN_HALF=2 / GAUSS_SIGMA=50 / FLAT_TRACKS)
world.description: Built ranges equal the data ranges, so the flattening is in the data, not in track.js: us-2012 elev range 20.6 m (real circuit ~41 m; the T1 hill is a 300 m feature that the 90 m DEM + 125 m median + 50 m Gaussian smear away), mc-1929 54.0 m with 17.7 % grades (real ~42 m, max ~10-12 %), us-2023 25.3 m with 8.7 % grades although the Las Vegas Strip circuit is nearly level (it is not in FLAT_TRACKS, unlike sg-2008 / sa-2021 / us-2022). The known leftovers are therefore confirmed, and Las Vegas is a new one.
world.failureScenario: COTA cockpit views c1/c2 (T1-T2 area) show a gently rolling road instead of the 40 m climb to T1; Las Vegas shows hills that do not exist.
world.suggestedFix: Add us-2023 to FLAT_TRACKS; for COTA (and other tracks with sharp hills) use a lower-smoothing profile or hand-corrected control heights; reduce Monaco's amplitude (MAX_SLOPE lower or a per-track scale).
world.evidence: Probe verify-world/elev.js (out/elev.log) re-derives the raw Copernicus GLO-90 samples from tools/elevation-cache.json. The flattening is mostly in the DEM itself, not the smoothing: us-2012 raw range 23 m, elev[] 20.6 m. mc-1929 raw 59 m, elev 54.0 m, built grade 17.7 %. us-2023 raw 30 m, elev 25.3 m, built grade 8.7 %. Checked against independent bare-earth terrain models. verify-world/usgs.js (USGS 3DEP EPQS, every 50 m, out/usgs.log): COTA real range 31.1 m with a 12.2 % climb to T1 (T1 at +28.2 m; game +17.0 m, max 7.5 %). Wikipedia quotes 41 m and >11 %, so COTA is too flat. Las Vegas real range is 16.1 m with a max 100 m grade of 3.0 %; the game has 24.6 m and 7.3 % (8.7 % built), with humps up to +9.6 m (e.g. s=3800: game 20.7 vs real 12.2). So Las Vegas is too hilly, but it is NOT level: the reviewer's premise and the FLAT_TRACKS fix are wrong, because FLAT_TRACKS scales the range down to 4 m. verify-world/ign-monaco.js (IGN RGE ALTI, out/ign-monaco.log): Monaco real range 41.5 m vs the game's 53.9 m, rms error 8.6 m. The error is worse than 'exaggerated': the harbour-front stretch at s~1080-1480 m is 2-7 m in IGN but 28-31 m in the game. The raw DSM there reads 21-52 m (buildings), so the game has a nonexistent ~17 % drop of ~20 m into Rascasse (s~1450-1600, the track's max grade). COTA and Monaco are listed as known leftovers in CLAUDE.md; Las Vegas is new.
world.verifiedFix: In tools/build-tracks.mjs, replace the Copernicus DSM with bare-earth terrain models where free APIs exist (both answered from this machine): USGS 3DEP EPQS for the US circuits (us-2012, us-2023, us-2022, us-1909, us-1956) and IGN RGE ALTI (data.geopf.fr altimetrie, resource ign_rge_alti_wld) for Monaco and the French tracks. Use lighter smoothing for DTM input (median off or 3 samples, Gaussian sigma ~15-20 m) so COTA's T1 climb survives. Where a tunnel makes a DTM read the ground above the road (Monaco tunnel), add hand control heights. Do not add us-2023 to FLAT_TRACKS (it has a real 16 m gentle slope). If no new source is allowed, give us-2023 heavier smoothing without the 4 m scale-down; a Monaco amplitude scale alone would not fix the fake harbour hill.

world.title: Kerbs and edge lines are decided before the pit lane exists, so kerb paint is drawn across the pit-lane taper asphalt where the taper runs through a kerbed bend (Monaco)
world.description: lineMask / kerbMask use wallOff and roomRoad as they were before the pit lane is laid out; the pit asphalt strip (pitStrip at Y_ROAD) is then added under them, but the kerb strips (Y_PAINT, higher) stay. On Monaco (60 km/h lane through the bend) 19 red kerb triangles lie on the pit taper asphalt at lane samples 1-22 and 133-137; on 13 other tracks 1-3 kerb triangles overlap the first/last taper sample. Also at k=0 / k=K the lane asphalt is a 0.6 m sliver (P.ao = halfW+0.6) that starts with a step.
world.failureScenario: Enter the Monaco pit lane: red/white kerb blocks lie on the pit-lane surface inside the taper.
world.suggestedFix: Recompute kerbMask/lineMask on the pit side over from..to after the pit layout (mask them out where pit.paved is true), and start the taper strip at P.ao = halfW (no 0.6 m step) or fade PIT_OUT_GAP in with f.
world.evidence: Code order in track.js confirms the claim. kerbMask/lineMask are computed at 504-532, before the pit layout (534-723). The pit asphalt is drawn at Y_ROAD (880) while kerbs stay at Y_PAINT in the paint mesh (polygonOffset -2), so they render on top. Probe verify-world/kerb-taper.js (out/kerb-taper.log) counts red kerb triangles in the kerb band (halfW..halfW+1.3) whose centroid is on pit.paved asphalt. Monaco has 19 at lane samples k=1..22 and 133..137 (K=139). 13 other tracks have 1-6 each, at the first or last taper samples (ae-2009 6, ca-1978 3, az-2016/de-1932/de-1927 2, the rest 1). The lane asphalt beyond the road edge is 0.59 m wide at k=0 and k=1, so the 0.6 m sliver/step claim is correct but negligible. Kerbs are visual only (no js module other than track.js references kerbs), so nothing affects physics. It is visible mainly at the Monaco taper (reviewer render probe-mc-1929-taper.png).
world.verifiedFix: Kerb strips are pushed at track.js 760-761, after the `if (pitL)` block at 711, so the mask can simply be edited there: for k in 0..P.L on side sd, clear kerbMask[sd][from+k] where P.ao[k] > halfW[i] + 0.05. Optionally start the taper asphalt at the road edge by fading PIT_OUT_GAP in with f (P.ao = P.lo + f*PIT_OUT_GAP + g*(bdp - PIT_OUT_GAP)) to remove the 0.6 m step.

world.title: groundY skips the verge beside the pit complex: points 30.5-41 m from the centreline get terrain height while the rendered skirt is higher
world.description: groundY returns terrainAt(x, z) when n.dist > WALL_DIST + WALL_THICK + SKIRT_W + 2 = 30.5 m. With the pit complex the outer wall foot is at up to ~25.6 m and its skirt (SKIRT_W 16) reaches ~41 m, so between 30.5 and 41 m the function disagrees with the drawn skirt mesh (probe: Spa 1.57 m, Zandvoort 0.44 m). scenery.js places trees (gY - 0.25), boards, posts and building bases from groundY, so objects behind the garages can float or sink by that amount.
world.failureScenario: At Spa, a tree or marshal post placed 32-40 m from the centreline behind the pit building stands up to 1.6 m above/below the rendered ground.
world.suggestedFix: Use the per-sample outer wall: early-out only when n.dist > max(wallOuter[...]) + SKIRT_W + 2 (compute the maximum once), or per side skO[sd][u] + skU[sd][u].
world.evidence: The code claim holds: track.js 1267 early-outs to terrainAt when n.dist > 30.5 m, while the pit side's wallOuter reaches ~25.6 m and its skirt reaches up to ~41 m. This violates the README v3 contract ('matches the rendered terrain mesh'). The magnitude and consequences are overstated, though. Probe verify-world/groundy.js (out/groundy.log) ray-casts the built 'ground' mesh (terrain plus skirts, highest hit) on a lattice 26-46 m out on the pit side. It also checks every scenery object recorded with F1.SCENERY_DEBUG. Worst rendered-minus-groundY per track is 0.14-0.68 m (br-1940 0.68, my-1999 0.61, jp-1962 0.55, hu-1986 0.52; Spa 0.33 m, not 1.57 m), always at 31-32 m from the centreline. Mismatch is 0 inside 30.5 m, and there is none at Monaco or Zandvoort. The reviewer's 1.57 m came from comparing the centreline height with the terrain, not the skirt with the terrain. Because groundY = terrain <= rendered = max(skirt, terrain), objects can only sink, never float. No tree, board, post or pole on the pit side has a point off by more than 0.2 m. Only a few building corners are off (pit/building, max 0.28 m), and those buildings already extend 1.5 m below their lowest ground sample, so nothing is visible.
world.verifiedFix: Low priority, one line: replace the constant with the real maximum. Compute once after the pit layout, e.g. var GY_EARLY = max over both sides and all i of (skO[side][i] + skU[side][i]) + 2, or max(wallOuter) + SKIRT_W + 2, and use it at line 1267. This makes groundY match the mesh everywhere, as the contract requires.
